name: Nullframe Ghost Balaclava — Port-Open Cut
description: A close-fit balaclava in matte signal-absorbing charcoal stretch-knit, leaving only the eyes exposed. Precision-cut port access panels at the occipital and temporal positions are finished with flat-lock seams and sit flush when unoccupied — no sagging or bunching. A secondary half-face filter layer is integral, not removable. The fabric has a faint crosshatch texture visible only at close range.
functionality: Neural-port access panels allow BCI plug-in without removal. Low-emissivity lining reduces thermal signature slightly. Integrated filter handles particulate and light chemical exposure. Fits snugly under helmets or hoods without bunching.
what_it_says: You move through spaces where being seen is a liability, and your chrome is not decorative.
worn_by: Tier 3 night workers with BCI rigs
story_hooks: Nullframe's port-open panels are cut to a spec that matches Axiom Defense neural jack placements exactly — either a coincidence or someone inside Axiom fed the pattern to a street label.
A Tier 4 compliance officer was found wearing one during an internal audit — the footage shows her plugging into a terminal she had no clearance for.
Three different operatives from competing firms showed up to the same location wearing identical Nullframe balaclavas on the same night. None of them know how that happened.
related_entities: Meridian Munitions Compact Machine Pistol CMP-4 'Jackrabbit'

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting balaclava that clings to the skull and neck like a second skin. Only the eyes are visible; the rest of the face, jaw, and throat are completely covered. Two subtle rectangular port panels—one at the back of the head, one at the temple—are barely perceptible unless you know to look for them. The overall effect is ghostly and minimalist, suggesting someone either augmented, security-conscious, or operating below the grid.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight throughout. The stretch-knit conforms precisely to head and neck anatomy with no excess fabric. Ports lay absolutely flush against the scalp when sealed, creating an unbroken silhouette.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte signal-absorbing charcoal stretch-knit (synthetic wool blend with RF-dampening weave)
physical_description.texture: Smooth to the touch with a faint, almost imperceptible crosshatch pattern visible only under direct close inspection. Slightly tacky matte finish that doesn't reflect light. The fabric is breathable but dense.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal matte black, no patterns or accents. Completely monochromatic. Port seams are barely distinguishable from the surrounding fabric.
physical_description.closures: None visible. The balaclava likely pulls on over the head and stays in place via compression. Port panels are friction-fit or magnetic-sealed; no mechanical closures.
distinctive_features: Precision-cut port access panels at occipital (back of skull) and temporal (temple) positions
Flat-lock seams on port panels for zero-snag edges
Eye openings only—no mouth or nose exposure
Ports flush when unoccupied, no sagging or bunching
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4–5 street-grade / sub-grade. Indicates someone actively hiding from surveillance, data harvesting, or corpo facial recognition. Not luxury, but purposeful and engineered.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by datarunnners, resistance operatives, augmentation technicians, and anyone wanting to disappear from the scanning infrastructure. The ports suggest someone regularly interfacing with external systems—neural jacks, optics patches, or diagnostic rigs. Street culture, anti-corpo posture, possibly medical or military-adjacent.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly worn. This is a precision piece, so it's maintained in good condition. May show faint wear at the eye openings from repeated donning/doffing. Odor buildup is common given the sealed design.
